title: Headache

rationale.Physical Exam: Heart / Cardiovascular: Hypertensive emergency → assess for LVH, S4, new murmurs.
rationale.Physical Exam: Neuro / Psych: Headache + visual changes — assess for focal deficits, altered mental status.
rationale.Physical Exam: Fundoscopy: Papilledema, retinal hemorrhages, cotton wool spots, AV nicking — signs of end-organ damage.
rationale.BMP / CMP: Creatinine — assess for acute kidney injury from hypertensive damage.
rationale.CT head without contrast: Rule out intracranial hemorrhage if focal neuro deficits or AMS.
rationale.IV Labetalol / Nicardipine / Clevidipine: IV antihypertensive. Reduce MAP by ≤25% in first hour. Goal DBP 100-105 over 2-6h. Do NOT rapidly normalize BP.
rationale.Admit to ICU: Hypertensive emergency requires ICU for continuous BP monitoring and IV therapy.
rationale.Short-acting nifedipine PO: Rapid, uncontrollable hypotension → cerebral and coronary hypoperfusion → stroke and MI. NEVER use short-acting nifedipine for hypertensive emergency.
rationale.Rapid BP normalization to 120/80: Reduce MAP by ≤25% in first hour. Rapid normalization causes cerebral hypoperfusion (loss of autoregulation). Goal DBP 100-105 over 2-6 hours.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with severe headache, blurred vision, and severely elevated blood pressure (>180/120). This is a hypertensive emergency — severe hypertension WITH evidence of acute end-organ damage (headache/visual changes suggesting cerebral involvement, possible papilledema, retinal hemorrhages). Must be distinguished from hypertensive urgency (severe HTN without end-organ damage — manage with oral meds as outpatient). Workup: fundoscopy (papilledema, hemorrhages, exudates), ECG (LVH, ischemia), CXR (pulmonary edema, aortic dissection signs), UA (proteinuria, hematuria), BMP (elevated Cr — renal damage), cardiac enzymes, CT head if focal neuro deficits. Treatment: IV antihypertensives in ICU — reduce MAP by no more than 25% in first hour (too rapid reduction causes cerebral/coronary hypoperfusion). Labetalol IV, nicardipine, or clevidipine. Goal: reduce DBP to 100-105 over 2-6 hours. Do NOT use short-acting nifedipine (risk of rapid uncontrollable hypotension).
